messages:
sarah: quick idea — we keep seeing partner/internal service jobs blow past per-key caps and then start retry storms. proposing a "safety net" that allows a tiny, audited burst for keys flagged internal/service or whitelisted partners.

mike: +1 to preventing downstream outages. what's the safety net shape? short time window or token budget?

sarah: time-boxed + token budget. example: allow up to 120s of burst or 5k extra tokens/minute, whichever comes first. every override creates an audit event.

devon: cautious here — we could introduce a DOS vector. need per-src-id limits so a single producer can't exhaust the budget. also require whitelisting.

raul: agree with devon. only for keys with metadata tag `internal:service=true` OR partners explicitly opt-in via console. plus IP/source checks.

sarah: draft config snippet (for discussion):

```
quota_safety_net:
  enabled: true
  allowed_burst_seconds: 120
  extra_tokens_per_minute: 5000
  max_tokens_per_src_per_minute: 1000
  whitelist_tags: ["internal:service"]
  require_audit: true
```

mike: looks good. can we make the lifecycle automatic? e.g., safety net triggers, then exponential backoff on subsequent requests.

sarah: yes — internal runtime will inject backoff headers and increment `quota.override.count`. we'll add `quota.override.duration_ms` and `quota.override.reason` metrics.

infra-bot: deploy queued: feature/quotas/safety-net -> staging :rocket:

devon: we should also expose a per-key timeline in the console: override events, who/what triggered them, and an action to revoke whitelist.

hannah: I can mock the UX. plan: per-key settings panel with a \"Safety net\" toggle, plus an events timeline and a link to the audit log.

sarah: great. security: any blockers for partner keys? tagging @security for signoff on audit retention and logging granularity.

security: we'll need request-level audit payloads for overrides: request_id, origin, triggering_key_id, model, token_counts, and an HSM/KMS reference for key operations. retention policy TBD but likely 90 days for override logs.

raul: also propose a hard stop if overrides for a key exceed 10k extra tokens in 24h — triggers manual review and temporary disable.

mike: rollout plan: staging deploy this week, internal services only in canary next week, then opt-in partners by console toggle after monitoring.

sarah: agreed. I'll open an RFC and a PR for the runtime changes + metric names. test harness will simulate a burst pattern and ensure counters and backoff work.

devon: metric names suggestion: `quota.override.count`, `quota.override.duration_ms`, `quota.override.tokens` and `quota.override.src_exhausted`.

sarah: adding that to the spec. also propose that override events include a `trigger_score` so we can tune false positives.

hannah: UX question — do we surface estimated cost impact of overrides in the console? could help partners decide to opt-in.

mike: useful. show an estimated tokens->cost delta and a toggle for auto-notify on override.

sarah: final checklist: runtime patch + metrics, console mock + toggle, doc + partner opt-in flow, security signoff, staging deploy, internal canary. I'll coordinate and post the RFC link here when ready.

raul: no objections from infra.

mike: :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks everyone — opening RFC now.
